title: Decomposing Gauss-Wantzel into Five Verifiable Steps
content: The Gauss-Wantzel theorem reduces to verifying five logical steps for any candidate n. This file's header makes the decomposition explicit: (a) [ℚ(ζₙ):ℚ] = φ(n) — available in Mathlib as IsCyclotomicExtension.finrank; (b) cos(2π/n) generates the maximal real subfield ℚ(ζₙ)⁺ — geometric fact needing assembly; (c) [ℚ(cos 2π/n):ℚ] = φ(n)/2 — follows from (a)+(b); (d) n-gon constructible ↔ [ℚ(cos 2π/n):ℚ] is a power of 2 — proved in OQ02; (e) φ(n)/2 = 2^k ↔ φ(n) = 2^{k+1} — **proved in this file**. Step (e) is the arithmetic bridge missing from OQ02-OQ03 that this extension supplies. The main contribution is that once Mathlib's cyclotomic field machinery is assembled for steps (a)-(d), step (e) is already formalized here and needs no additional work.
mathContext: Chain: $n$-gon constructible $\Leftrightarrow$ $[\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n):\mathbb{Q}] = \varphi(n)$ (Mathlib) $\Leftrightarrow$ $[\mathbb{Q}(\cos 2\pi/n):\mathbb{Q}] = \varphi(n)/2$ (real subfield) $\Leftrightarrow$ $\varphi(n)/2 = 2^k$ (OQ02) $\Leftrightarrow$ $\varphi(n) = 2^{k+1}$ (this file) $\Leftrightarrow$ $n = 2^a \cdot \prod p_i$ (Fermat primes).

title: The Arithmetic Bridge: φ(n)/2 = 2^(k−1) iff φ(n) = 2^k
content: Section I proves the key arithmetic bridge: totient_pow2_iff_half_pow2 (for n ≥ 3): φ(n) = 2^k iff φ(n)/2 = 2^j. The proof uses two helper lemmas. pow2_of_half_pow2: if 2 | m and m/2 = 2^k then m = 2^{k+1}, proved by rewriting m = 2·(m/2) using Nat.mul_div_cancel'. half_pow2_of_pow2: 2^{k+1}/2 = 2^k, proved by rewriting pow_succ then Nat.mul_div_cancel_left. totient_even_of_ge_three: 2 | φ(n) for n ≥ 3, proved by Nat.totient_even (which captures that -1 ∈ (ℤ/nℤ)* has order 2). The iff proof: (→) if φ(n) = 2^k with k ≥ 1 (ensured because totient is positive for n ≥ 1 and equals 1 only for n = 1,2), then φ(n)/2 = 2^{k-1}; (←) if φ(n)/2 = 2^j, use pow2_of_half_pow2 with totient_even_of_ge_three to get φ(n) = 2^{j+1}. The case k = 0 (φ(n) = 1) is ruled out for n ≥ 3 by totient_pos.
mathContext: For $n \geq 3$: $\varphi(n)$ is even (since $-1 \in (\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^*$ has order 2). Iff: $\varphi(n) = 2^k \Leftrightarrow \varphi(n)/2 = 2^{k-1}$. Key: $k \geq 1$ is forced because $\varphi(n) \geq 2$ for $n \geq 3$.
prerequisites: integer division exactness for powers of 2

title: Non-Constructibility via Odd Prime Divisors of φ(n)
content: Section II provides the non-constructibility criterion and applies it to all non-constructible n ≤ 50. not_totient_pow2_of_odd_prime_dvd: if prime p ≠ 2 divides φ(n), then TotientIsPow2 n is false. Proof: suppose φ(n) = 2^k; then p | 2^k; by Nat.Prime.dvd_of_dvd_pow: p | 2; since p is prime and p ≠ 2: contradiction. The applications follow a template: `not_totient_pow2_of_odd_prime_dvd (by decide) (by decide) (show q ∣ Nat.totient n by decide)`. For each non-constructible n, an explicit odd prime divisor is exhibited: e.g., for n=19: 3 | φ(19) = 18 (via `show 3 ∣ Nat.totient 19 by decide`); for n=23: 11 | φ(23) = 22; for n=29: 7 | φ(29) = 28; for n=47: 23 | φ(47) = 46. This approach — exhibiting a single odd prime factor in φ(n) — gives one-line non-constructibility proofs for all 31 non-constructible n ≤ 50.
mathContext: Non-constructibility criterion: $\exists$ odd prime $p$ with $p \mid \varphi(n)$ $\Rightarrow$ $\varphi(n) \neq 2^k$. Contrapositive of: $\varphi(n) = 2^k$ $\Rightarrow$ all prime factors of $\varphi(n)$ are 2. Template: for $n = 19$, $\varphi(19) = 18 = 2 \cdot 3^2$, so $3 \mid \varphi(19)$.
prerequisites: φ(n) formula for primes and prime powers

title: Multiplicativity of TotientIsPow2: Products Preserve Powers of 2
content: Sections IV–V develop structural results for the totient function. totient_multiplicative wraps Nat.totient_mul: φ(mn) = φ(m)·φ(n) when gcd(m,n) = 1. totient_pow2_mul: if TotientIsPow2 m and TotientIsPow2 n and gcd(m,n) = 1, then TotientIsPow2 (m·n). Proof: φ(m) = 2^a, φ(n) = 2^b gives φ(mn) = 2^a · 2^b = 2^{a+b} by pow_add. The contrapositive not_totient_pow2_factor: if ¬TotientIsPow2 (m·n) then ¬TotientIsPow2 m ∨ ¬TotientIsPow2 n, proved by by_contra then push_neg and applying totient_pow2_mul. totient_pow2_prime_iff: for prime p, TotientIsPow2 p ↔ p-1 = 2^k. This is the Fermat prime characterization: p is a Fermat prime (p = 2^{2^j}+1) iff φ(p) = p-1 is a power of 2. Together these structural results explain why constructibility reduces to the prime factorization: n is constructible iff its odd prime factors are all Fermat primes and appear to the first power.
mathContext: $\varphi$ multiplicative: $\varphi(mn) = \varphi(m)\varphi(n)$ for $\gcd(m,n)=1$. Powers of 2 are closed under multiplication: $2^a \cdot 2^b = 2^{a+b}$. Fermat prime: $p$ is Fermat $\Leftrightarrow$ $p - 1 = 2^{2^j}$ for some $j$ $\Leftrightarrow$ $p - 1$ is a power of 2.

title: Complete n ∈ [3,50] Classification: 17 Constructible, 31 Not
content: Section VI completes the classification for all n from 3 to 50 not handled in the parent OQ02-OQ03 file. The constructible n in [3,50] are exactly: {3,4,5,6,8,10,12,15,16,17,20,24,30,32,34,40,48}. These are n = 2^a × (distinct Fermat primes from {3,5,17}): 3=3, 4=2², 5=5, 6=2×3, 8=2³, 10=2×5, 12=4×3, 15=3×5, 16=2⁴, 17=17, 20=4×5, 24=8×3, 30=2×15=2×3×5, 32=2⁵, 34=2×17, 40=8×5, 48=16×3. Note: 3×17=51 > 50, 5×17=85 > 50, 3×5×17=255 > 50, so no further Fermat prime products appear in range. The 31 non-constructible values each have an odd prime factor in φ(n) that is NOT 2, certified by exhibiting such a prime via `decide`. Key examples: φ(31) = 30 = 2×3×5 (3|30), φ(37) = 36 = 4×9 (3|36), φ(47) = 46 = 2×23 (23|46 — a large prime divisor).
prerequisites: Gauss-Wantzel: constructible iff Fermat prime structure

title: constructible_up_to_50: All 17 Constructible n-gons in One Theorem
content: The summary theorem constructible_up_to_50 packages all 17 TotientIsPow2 proofs into a single conjunction. The proof uses `refine ⟨⟨1, by decide⟩, ⟨1, by decide⟩, ..., ⟨4, by decide⟩⟩` — each TotientIsPow2 n is witnessed by the explicit exponent k with φ(n) = 2^k: TotientIsPow2 3 witnessed by k=1 (φ(3)=2=2¹), TotientIsPow2 17 by k=4 (φ(17)=16=2⁴), TotientIsPow2 48 by k=4 (φ(48)=16=2⁴). The conjunction theorem makes the complete classification a single statement that downstream users (e.g., an angle-trisection decision procedure) can import as one dependency. Importantly, this theorem does NOT cover n > 50; generalizing to all n requires either the Fermat prime structure theorem or an infinite enumeration, which remains an open problem (conditional on the infinitely-many-Fermat-primes question).
